In the worst case (no node sharing), transferring $n$ cells requires $80n$ bytes (16 bytes per cell + 64 bytes for unique nodes) [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly state that each cell stores 16 bytes (four node indices) and each node stores 16 bytes (three coordinates and one scalar value). They further explain that in the worst case of no node sharing, transferring n cells requires transferring the cell data (16n bytes) plus the node data for all unique nodes associated with those cells. Since a cell has 4 nodes, this results in 4 * 16n = 64n bytes for nodes. The total is 16n + 64n = 80n bytes. This matches the claim exactly.
